subject: Culture
title: The Bikini Revolution
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Bikini Revolution.

hook.text: When Louis Réard unveiled the bikini in 1946, no model would wear it. He hired a stripper instead.

buildup.text: He named it after Bikini Atoll, where atomic bombs were tested—predicting it would cause a cultural explosion.

discovery.text: Spain, Italy, and several US states banned the bikini. The Vatican called it sinful. Beach patrols measured fabric.

twist.text: By the 1960s, the bikini was mainstream. What scandalized one generation became the next generation's default.

climax.text: Today's debates about burkinis repeat the same pattern: authorities policing women's coverage in public spaces.

punchline.text: Too much skin or too little—someone's always measuring.

quiz.question: What was the bikini named after?
